title: Designing AI for Real Users: Accessibility Gaps in Retail AI Front-End

bias_targets.methodology: Practice-led qualitative analysis of retail AI interfaces (virtual try-on, conversational AI, personalized ranking) to identify accessibility barriers for differently abled users (e.g., blind, low-vision, neuro-divergent, motor-impaired), alongside proposals for adapting fairness metrics like task completion parity and error rate balance across ability groups.

Qualitative evaluation of how AI front-end design assumptions regarding interaction speed, phrasing norms, and familiarity with platform-specific visual cues and conventions implicitly marginalize older and younger users.
